source_text: Τοὺς μὲν οὖν ἐγκαταλεχθέντας τοῖς βαρβάροις καὶ μετ᾿ αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ αἰχμαλωσίᾳ ἐπελθόντας, ἐπιλαθομένους ὅτι ἦσαν Ποντικοὶ καὶ χριστιανοὶ, ἐκβαρβαρωθέντας δὲ ὡς καὶ φονεύειν τοὺς ὁμοφύλους ἢ ξύλῳ ἢ ἀγχόνῃ, ὑποδεικνῦναι δὲ ἢ ὁδοὺς ἢ οἰκίας ἀγνοοῦσι τοῖς βαρβάροις, καὶ τῆς ἀκροάσεως ἀπεῖρξαι δεῖ, μέχρις ἂν κοινῇ περὶ αὐτῶν τι δόξῃ συνελθοῦσι, τοῖς ἁγίοις, καὶ πρὸ αὐτῶν τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι.
thought_title: Treatment of apostate captives who turned against their own people
orientation: Gregory instructs the bishop on how to handle captives who defected to the barbarians, committed murder against fellow Christians, and guided the enemy; they must be excluded from the church's hearing pending a joint decision with the saints and the Holy Spirit.
pass_a_gloss: Those, on the one hand, having been left behind with the barbarians and having gone on with them in the captivity, having forgotten that they were Pontians and Christians, having become barbarized so as even to murder their fellow-tribesmen either with wood or with strangling, and showing either roads or houses unknown to the barbarians, and it is necessary to bar them from the hearing until some opinion might seem good to those assembled together with the holy ones, and before them to the holy Spirit.

choices.why: Passive participle of ἐγκαταλείπω; the captives were abandoned to the barbarians, not merely 'left' actively.
Compound verb ἐκβαρβαρόω indicates a thorough change into barbarous behavior; 'became barbarians' loses the process sense.
Specific term for people of the same tribe/race (Pontians); 'fellow Christians' is broader than the ethnic force here.
Instrumental datives; ξύλῳ means a wooden weapon/club, ἀγχόνῃ means strangling/noose. Keep both instruments distinct.
Present infinitive of ὑποδείκνυμι, concurrent with the other participles; 'pointing out' is possible but 'showing' covers roads and houses.
δεῖ + aorist infinitive expresses obligation; 'bar from the hearing' reflects ἀπείργω τῆς ἀκροάσεως (genitive of separation).

choices.term: μέχρις ἂν κοινῇ περὶ αὐτῶν τι δόξῃ συνελθοῦσι τοῖς ἁγίοις
choices.english: until some opinion might seem good to those assembled together with the holy ones
choices.why: μέχρις ἂν + aorist subjunctive δόξῃ; συνελθοῦσι dative plural participle 'to those having assembled'; κοινῇ 'jointly'.
rejected: until a common decision is reached

choices.english: and before them to the holy Spirit
choices.why: πρὸ with genitive 'before' in priority/order; the Holy Spirit precedes the saints in authority.
rejected: in the presence of the Holy Spirit

pass_b_english: I must address those who were enrolled among the barbarians and went on with them in captivity. They forgot that they were Pontians and Christians, and became thoroughly barbarized — so much so that they even murdered their fellow-tribesmen, whether with a club or by strangling. They also showed the barbarians roads and houses that had been unknown to them. These people must be barred from the hearing until some common decision about them might seem good to the saints assembled together, and before them to the Holy Spirit.

problems.quote: until some opinion might seem good to those assembled together with the holy ones
problems.source_quote: μέχρις ἂν κοινῇ περὶ αὐτῶν τι δόξῃ συνελθοῦσι, τοῖς ἁγίοις
problems.why: The saints themselves meet and decide together about these people. The English gives the decision to an unnamed group meeting 'with' the saints, and it drops 'about them'.
problems.fix: until the saints, meeting together, reach a common decision about them

problems.quote: those who were left behind with the barbarians
problems.source_quote: Τοὺς μὲν οὖν ἐγκαταλεχθέντας τοῖς βαρβάροις
problems.why: ἐγκαταλεχθέντας means enrolled or enlisted among the barbarians, not left behind with them. This hides that these people chose to join the invaders.
problems.fix: those who enrolled themselves among the barbarians
problems.ruling: ἐγκαταλεχθέντας is enrolled/listed among (ἐγκαταλέγω), not left behind; voluntary joining among βαρβάροις is lost.

problems.quote: went on with them in captivity
problems.source_quote: μετ᾿ αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ αἰχμαλωσίᾳ ἐπελθόντας
problems.why: ἐπελθόντας means attacked or invaded. These people joined the barbarians' raids during the captivity; they did not just travel along with them.
problems.fix: joined them in their raids at the time of the captivity
problems.ruling: ἐπελθόντας from ἐπέρχομαι means come against/raid, not merely accompany; hostile action in αἰχμαλωσίᾳ is softened.

edits.old: until some opinion might seem good to those assembled together with the holy ones
edits.new: until some common decision about them might seem good to the saints assembled together

edits.old: those who were left behind with the barbarians
edits.new: those who were enrolled among the barbarians

fixed: agency: fixed to saints as deciders, restoring κοινῇ as common and περὶ αὐτῶν as about them
enrolled: fixed to enrolled among because ἐγκαταλεχθέντας is from ἐγκαταλέγω, not left behind
raids: no edit — μετ᾿ αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ αἰχμαλωσίᾳ ἐπελθόντας has no object or word for raids, so went on with them correctly renders ἐπελθόντας with μετ᾿ αὐτῶν

last_rejected.quote: I must address those who were enrolled
last_rejected.why: Source has no verb of addressing the author; it opens a description of persons to exclude.
last_rejected.fix: As for those who were enrolled among the barbarians and went on with them in captivity,
last_rejected.ruling: 'I must address' is only a framing device that splits the long sentence. The ruling on 'Τοὺς μὲν οὖν ἐγκαταλεχθέντας' is still fully given; no meaning is lost or changed.

last_rejected.quote: I must address those who were enrolled
last_rejected.why: Greek's main requirement is that they be barred from the hearing, not that Gregory must discuss them.
last_rejected.fix: Those who … must be barred from the hearing until …
last_rejected.ruling: The English keeps 'ἀπεῖρξαι δεῖ' as 'These people must be barred from the hearing', so the main requirement and its 'must' are both kept.
